applicability: A float-to-bf16, float-to-fp16, or float-to-int8 conversion must match a torch reference.
A quantized stage is the precision bottleneck.
A kernel parameter, golden tensor, and real weight disagree on dtype.
directions: Write `pl.cast(x, pl.BF16, mode='rint')` or `pl.cast(x, pl.FP16, mode='rint')` when matching torch's narrowing.
Use `pl.cast(acc, pl.FP32, mode='none')` for a width-preserving accumulator move.
Quantize with `pl.cast(pl.mul(x_fp32, inv_scale), pl.INT8, mode='rint')` rather than casting to bf16 or fp16 first.
Cast an injected real weight to `TensorSpec.dtype` before running, and make kernel and golden output dtypes identical.
For per-channel weights, carry `weight_scale` per channel and use the same granularity in the kernel and golden.
effects: Wider intermediates improve accuracy but cost bandwidth and registers.
Per-channel or per-token quantization recovers dynamic range but adds scales and arithmetic.
A multi-hop cast may be the only lowering for a pair on a target, but it changes last-bit behavior.
invariants: `pl.cast` on a `Scalar` supports only the default mode; a non-default scalar rounding mode raises.
Some `(source, destination)` cast pairs are one instruction on one architecture and a chain on another.
A dtype mismatch can mis-read bytes or silently widen rather than raise.
The comparator may cast one side and hide a real narrowing if output dtypes differ.
The default `round` is not torch's tie behavior.
principle: `pl.cast(input, target_type, mode=...)` accepts `none` (0, a width-preserving or reinterpret move), `rint` (1, round-to-nearest ties-to-even), `round` (2, ties-away-from-zero, the default), `floor` (3), `ceil` (4), `trunc` (5), and `odd` (6). Torch's `.to(dtype)` uses round-to-nearest ties-to-even, so a narrowing cast intended to match torch must pass `mode='rint'`; the default differs on exact ties. Use `rint` for fp32-to-bf16, fp32-to-fp16, fp32-to-int8 quantizers, and integer dequantization that needs rounded conversion. Use `none` for an Acc-to-Vec or other width-preserving move. Use `trunc` or `floor` for float-to-int index or lane math, never ties-away, which can jump an index. Keep activations and intermediates at the highest precision that is free, usually fp32, and narrow only where a bf16, fp16, or int8 consumer requires it. Never cast through an intermediate narrowing: fp32-to-uint8 or fp32-to-int8 should quantize directly from fp32, not via bf16 or fp16, because the intermediate hop discards mantissa bits before quantization. The same applies to dequantization: go from the integer to fp32, not through fp16. PyPTO has no implicit promotion; every width change needs an explicit cast. A narrow op may lower to one hardware `pto.tcvt` or a chain of conversions depending on target; a multi-hop chain can differ from a directly rounded conversion by one destination ULP. Match every input and output dtype across kernel, golden, and real weights. A real weight injected into a kernel must be cast to the kernel's declared spec dtype. Cube matmul honors the stored dtype of each operand: fp32 x fp32, fp16 x fp16, bf16 x bf16, and int8 paths are distinct. Do not assume the whole model is bf16; match the matmul precision to the stored weight and make the golden do the same. Quantization is a scheme, not a constant: per-tensor versus per-channel or per-token scales, symmetric versus asymmetric, activation scale from the actual dynamic range, and RNE on the scaled value. Measure the error distribution rather than a single pass/fail.
questions: The exact one-ULP difference introduced by a target-specific multi-hop cast requires compiling and comparing the concrete pair.
risks: Using the default `round` for a torch-matching narrowing cast and chasing a tie-only mismatch.
Casting fp32 to bf16 before int8 quantization, losing mantissa bits before the quantizer.
Letting the golden stay fp32 where the kernel narrows to bf16, under-reporting the kernel's real error.
Assuming every matmul is bf16 while a real weight is stored fp32 or fp16.
summary: Most apparent kernel errors are avoidable precision losses: the wrong cast rounding mode, a dtype that silently widened or narrowed, a two-hop cast, or a golden that computes a different order. Keep intermediates in the widest free type, cast once at the consuming boundary, and align kernel, golden, and stored weights.
title: Rounding Modes, Dtype Alignment, and Quantization Precision
